label: Late-episode GO: choosing a2 again after a2->S2 common win that followed a loss
explanation: Sparse feature that fires only at GO and only in the last ~10 trials of an episode (96% of mass in trials 90-99, none before trial 80; equivalently value-head output < 5.2). Every activation has prev_reward == 1, the upcoming choice a2 (model_act a2, strongly negative choice logit), and, where known, the previous trial was a2 -> S2 common. It never fires after a rare transition, after an unrewarded trial, when choosing a1, or at D1/D2. Within that set it prefers a reward that comes right after a loss (the trial two back unrewarded); consecutive wins are often silent. Recorded predicate: GO, previous trial a common rewarded transition, two-back trial unrewarded, choosing a2, ep_trial >= 90 (dev P 0.64 R 0.69 F1 0.66, mass 0.79). The looser version without the two-back-loss condition (tv(prev_reward,-1) != 1) has mass recall 0.95 but P 0.41. Misses are mostly at window rel -3, where the reward history is cut off. Only observed variables are used, plus the agent own upcoming choice (action == 2), which is allowed. Precision stays limited: many matching steps are silent and magnitude varies without a clear driver, so this is only a partial explanation. It looks like an end-of-episode, win-stay-on-a2 signal.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over trial before (GO: a2 S1 u, a2 S2 u, ?) and last trial (GO: a2 S2 r, ?); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=9, phase=GO & ep_dec=8, rel=-3.
